title: Trump’s metaphorical shrug after the midterms | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

One of the biggest takeaways from Democrats’ historic rout in the 2026 midterm elections was that voters saw President Donald Trump as out of touch and uninterested in their plights.

TheCNN Voter Pollshowed 63% of voters said Trump prioritized his personal interests over the country’s interests. And 64% said Trump did not “fight for people like you.”

The president has spent the two weeks since the election doing the opposite of course correcting. Indeed, he seems bent on proving that voters were right.

Over the past 14 days, Trump has doubled down on his dismissal of Americans’ economic problems, shrugged off a series of major systemic and governmental failures, and gone right on focusing like a laser on his gilded renovations of Washington and the White House.

The most striking comment came early Tuesday when Trump landed in the Philippines.

Asked about a series of recent events that have rocked Americans’ everyday lives — a full ground stop at airports and outages and software problems from Microsoft, Chase Bank and United Airlines — Trump effectively turned himself intothe “This is fine” meme.

“It’s life,” Trump said. “When you’re big and powerful and have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine.”

The response exemplified the metaphorical shrug Trump has offered in recent days about the FAA ground stop and the growing Nvidia scandal.

After it was reported that then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang hadan affairwith a woman who is suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence — and whose company is suspected of illicitly funneling AI chips to China — Trump repeatedly downplayed the story.

He’s also cast doubt on the idea that Alice Huang was a spy. (The US intelligence community is still working to understand the relationship between the Chinese businesswoman and the Chinese government.)

And Trump responded to aremarkable spat between two of his Cabinet secretariesby suggesting it was a simple philosophical disagreement about confronting China.

He also downplayed the severity of the potential Chinese espionage, saying, “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”

Just to underscore — asCNN’s Stephen Collinson does— this isn’t just a sex or even a corporate scandal. This is about whether the leading US adversary compromised the most valuable company in the United States, which is vital to winning the AI race against China. (China has denied the reports.)

And it’s also a scandal that has cost many Americans a significant amount of money, thanks to the tumbling Nvidia stock.

Trump’s response to the ground stop has been similar.

Despite it snarling travel throughout the weekend and leaving travelers apoplectic, Trump said next to nothing about the ground stop for two days. And even when he finally weighed in on Sunday, he merely issued someperfunctory-soundingsocial media postsasking Congress for more money.

Speaking of money, Trump has done almost nothing to change his dismissive posture toward Americans’ economic concerns that cost the GOP so dearly.

In a social media post on Monday, he again claimed that the economy was “booming!” This is despite the Voter Poll showing just 2% of voters in the midterms saying the economy was “excellent” and three-quarters saying it was “not so good” or “poor.”

(Trump spent more than a year telling people that they were wrong and that the economywas, in fact, in a new golden age, but they clearly didn’t feel it.)

At the same time, Trump has downplayed his own wealth growth over the last two years (largely thanks to his ethically dubious cryptocurrency venture) by claiming in a “60 Minutes” interview after the election that “everyone” has done well and pointing to the stock market.

Except many Americans don’t hold substantial amounts of stock, andwage growth hasn’t kept pace with inflationfor most of 2026. The CNN Voter Poll showed just 17% of voters said their families’ financial situation was better than two years ago.

And finally, there’s Trump’s continued focus on his renovations in Washington — things like the White House ballroom, his proposed triumphal arch and overhaul of the golf course in East Potomac Park.

When challenged Monday on whether he was too focused on such things, Trump became angry, insisting he spends only “10 minutes a day” on the subject and that it “doesn’t cost money.”

But it’s clearly a priority for him. The ballroom was Trump’s first public event after his party’s drubbing two weeks ago (after a stop at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool the day before the election). He’s fighting legal battles so he can build the arch and renovate the golf course. On Saturday he posted more than half a dozen times withimages of East Potomac Park, suggesting it was in disrepair. And on Monday, heposted imagesof gold statues.

In other words, he seems rather preoccupied.

“It was sort of mentioned a little bit during the campaign about, ‘Why does Trump spend time on the White House?’” Trump said during his ballroom visit the day after the election. “Well, first of all, it’s very little time. Second of all, I like it, it’s good. For me it’s relaxing. … I love construction.”

Here is Trump doing a lot of the things he was doing before the election and that polls suggested were probably hurting him and the GOP.

AJuly CNN pollshowed 73% of Americans said that Trump was not in touch with the problems that Americans face. ASeptember CNN pollshowed 74% said Trump hadn’t paid enough attention to the country’s most important problems.

Andpre-election AP-NORC pollingshowed just 23% said Trump prioritized the country “a lot” and 11% said he prioritized “people like me” that much — compared to majorities who said he prioritized his and his friends’ and family’s business interests “a lot.”

While before the election Trump and those around them could delude themselves into believing that maybe his bizarre political strategies and focus on unpopular policies didn’t matter that much, the 2026 election results should have disabused anybody of those notions.

But recognizing the problem is only a small part of resolving it. The other part is getting a stubborn 80-year-old man whose aides appear allergic to questioning him to change his stripes.

And Trump seems to have no interest in that.
